title: 90-Day Reporting in Thailand (TM47): How and When to Report
summary: If you stay in Thailand for more than 90 days in a row, you must tell immigration your address every 90 days. It is free, takes a few minutes online or in person, and missing it costs 2,000 THB.
seoTitle: Thailand 90-Day Report (TM47): Deadlines, Online Filing and Fines
seoDescription: Who must file the 90-day report in Thailand, the 15-day window, how to report online, in person or by post, and the fines for being late.

sections.heading: What the 90-day report is
paragraphs: Foreigners who stay in Thailand for more than 90 days in a row must notify immigration of their address every 90 days. The form is called TM47.
It is not an extension. It doesn't change how long you may stay. It only confirms where you live.

sections.heading: Who must report
paragraphs: Anyone on a long stay: retirement or marriage extensions, O-A, business and work visas, students, DTV holders and others, once you have been in Thailand for 90 days in a row.
list: Children must report too. From the age of 15 a child should report themselves.
Tourists who leave before day 90 don't need to report.

sections.heading: When to report
paragraphs: You can report from 15 days before the due date until 7 days after it. Your next due date is printed on the receipt you get each time.
The count starts again at day 1 every time you enter Thailand, including when you return on a re-entry permit.
Applying for your first extension of stay counts as a 90-day report.

sections.heading: How to report
list: Online at tm47.immigration.go.th. You get an approval by email. If the system rejects you, report in person instead.
In person at the immigration office for your address. Bring your passport, TM47 and copies of your passport pages.
Through someone else, with your signed form and a letter of authorisation.
By registered post. The letter must arrive at least 15 days before the due date. Include a stamped return envelope.

sections.heading: Documents for an in-person or postal report
list: Copies of your passport photo page, current visa or extension and latest entry stamp
Your previous 90-day receipt, if you have one
Proof of address, such as your rental contract or house book

sections.heading: Fines
paragraphs: Reporting late costs 2,000 THB. If you are caught without having reported at all, the fine is 4,000 THB. Once you are late, you must pay the fine in person. You can't report by post.

faqs.q: Does leaving Thailand reset the count?
faqs.a: Yes. Every time you enter Thailand, the count starts again at day 1.

faqs.q: Is the 90-day report the same as TM30?
faqs.a: No. TM30 is the address notification your landlord files when you arrive at a place. The 90-day report is your own duty every 90 days.
No, it's free if you report on time. The late fine is 2,000 THB.

faqs.q: Can an agent do it for me?
faqs.a: Yes. Someone can report for you with your signed form and a letter of authorisation.
